passage:
"You laughed so loudly when you fell!" Darshan said, dropping onto the canteen bench beside Urmila. "You looked so confident."
"Confident?" She stared at him. "Darshan, I wanted the floor to swallow me. Forty people watched me trip on my own bag strap."
"But you got up, took a bow and everyone clapped."
"That's because I laughed first. If I hadn't, I think I'd have run out." She rubbed her elbow. "It was half funny, half horrible."
"I honestly thought you didn't care."
"I care about everything. That's the problem."
Darshan grinned and pushed his fries toward her. "Next time, I'll sit close. Deal?" She took one. "Deal."

qa.q: What did Urmila trip on?
qa.a: She tripped on her own bag strap.

qa.q: What was Urmila feeling as she laughed loudly?
qa.a: She was embarrassed and afraid of looking foolish, and the laugh helped cover it and gave her relief, though part of it was truly funny.

qa.q: What could Darshan do next time a friend slips in public?
qa.a: He could stay close and check in afterwards, because a big laugh may be covering embarrassment rather than showing confidence.

qa.q: How did the onlookers likely read Urmila's laughter?
qa.a: They read it as confidence and clapped, so they missed how uncomfortable she felt.

grounding: A teen laughs loudly after a slip in front of others to cover embarrassment, and others read it as confidence.

passage: In Class 11 I once walked into the glass door of the physics lab in front of everyone. It made an actual thud. I remember the exact second: silence, then my own voice booming with laughter before anyone else's. I even said "Ta-da!" and waved. People cheered. Francis, who sat next to me, gave me a thumbs up and told me afterwards I was the most relaxed person he'd ever seen. I nodded as though I was. But my ears were burning, and I went to the toilets and stood there for five minutes, hands under cold water, feeling foolish and relieved at the same time. I still laugh first when I slip. I just know now what that laugh is. - Samir

qa.q: What did Samir walk into in front of everyone?
qa.a: Samir walked into the glass door of the physics lab.

qa.q: What was Samir feeling while standing in the toilets?
qa.a: Samir felt foolish and relieved, since the loud laugh had covered the embarrassment and the room had accepted it.

qa.q: What could Samir tell Francis in order to be understood?
qa.a: Samir could say that the laugh was covering embarrassment and that the relaxed look was not the whole story.

qa.q: How did Francis see Samir after the slip?
qa.a: He saw a very relaxed person, so he misread the laugh as confidence.

grounding: A teen laughs loudly after a slip to cover embarrassment, others read it as confidence, and the laugh may be relief.

passage:
Annual Day note - Zainab (Class 9 teacher), Saturday
During the group dance, Urmila slipped on the edge of the stage and landed on one knee in front of about four hundred parents. There was a gasp. Then Urmila threw her head back and laughed, really loudly, got up, and finished the dance with a big grin.
Afterwards several parents and students praised her: "So confident!" "She didn't care at all!"
I wasn't sure. Her laugh had been a bit too loud, and she'd glanced at her friends in the wings before laughing.
In the green room, I asked her quietly, "That was brave. How are you feeling about the slip?"
Her smile dropped. "Ma'am, I wanted to disappear. I laughed so nobody would laugh at me first."
I told her that was a smart, quick move, and that she was allowed to feel embarrassed too. She laughed again, smaller and real.

qa.q: How many parents were watching when Urmila slipped?
qa.a: About four hundred parents.

qa.q: What feelings were behind Urmila's loud laugh?
qa.a: Urmila felt embarrassed and afraid of being laughed at, so she laughed first to cover it.

qa.q: What did Zainab do that helped?
qa.a: She asked quietly and privately how Urmila felt, and accepted both the quick cover and the embarrassment underneath.

qa.q: How did the parents who praised her read the laugh?
qa.a: They read it as confidence and not caring, missing the embarrassment behind it.

grounding: The teacher's note shows a teenager laughing loudly after a slip to cover embarrassment, which others read as confidence.

passage:
Wednesday
In English today, I read aloud and said "epi-tome" instead of "epitome." Like "tome," like a big book. Someone at the back snorted.
And I laughed. So loudly. Like it was the funniest thing ever. "Epi-TOME! What a word!" Everyone laughed with me, and Ma'am smiled and corrected me.
Sabina said at break, "You're so chill. I'd have died."
Diary, I'm not chill. My face was burning the whole time. I laughed because if I laughed first, they'd be laughing with me, not at me. And honestly part of it was relief too, that the class laughed nicely.
I want to tell Sabina the truth. Maybe tomorrow. She'd probably get it. She went red for a week after tripping on sports day.
- Vandana

qa.q: What word did Vandana mispronounce?
qa.a: "Epitome."

qa.q: What was Vandana feeling while laughing so loudly?
qa.a: Vandana felt embarrassed and afraid of being laughed at, with some relief when the class laughed kindly.

qa.q: What might happen if Vandana tells Sabina the truth?
qa.a: Sabina would likely understand, since she has felt embarrassed herself, and Vandana wouldn't have to pretend to be chill.

qa.q: How did Sabina read Vandana's laugh?
qa.a: Sabina read it as confidence and being chill, not seeing the embarrassment behind it.

grounding: The diary shows a teenager laughing loudly to cover embarrassment, and a friend reading it as confidence.

passage: At the kasba school's annual sports day, the ground was still slick from the night's rain. Ujjwal was running the last leg of the relay, the whole school lined up along the rope, when his foot went out from under him and he slid three metres on his back through the mud, baton still in his fist. For a second there was total silence. Then Ujjwal sat up and laughed. Loudly, head thrown back, waving the muddy baton like a flag. Everyone laughed with him. "He's so confident," someone near Arohi said. "I'd have died." Arohi wasn't so sure. His laugh went on a beat too long, and his ears were bright red under the mud. Later, rinsing his shirt at the handpump, Ujjwal said to her without looking up, "If I didn't laugh first, they'd have laughed at me instead." Then, quieter: "Also, honestly, I was just glad nothing was broken."

qa.q: What was Ujjwal holding when he slid?
qa.a: Ujjwal still had the baton in his fist.

qa.q: What feelings might Ujjwal's loud laugh have been covering?
qa.a: Most likely embarrassment and a fear of being laughed at, shown by the red ears and a laugh that went on too long; it was also partly relief that nothing was broken.

qa.q: How could Arohi support Ujjwal?
qa.a: Arohi could keep checking in quietly, as at the handpump, and avoid bringing up the fall in front of others, since the laugh was protection.

qa.q: Why might the classmate near Arohi read the laugh as confidence?
qa.a: From a distance a loud laugh and a waved baton look carefree, so that classmate missed the red ears and the too-long laugh.

grounding: It shows a teenager laughing loudly after a public slip, others reading it as confidence, while it covered embarrassment, fear of mockery and relief.
